verdict_rationale: resolveIdBySlug now returns a discriminated SlugResolveResult (id|not_found|ambiguous) instead of `string|null`. All 5 call sites in src/http/assistant.ts (lines 625, 651, 765, 836, 1036) handle all three members — verified by reading each call site plus tsc: because the union is discriminated and the code narrows via `if (kind==='not_found') return; if (kind==='ambiguous') return;` before touching `.id`, a missing branch would fail to compile (not_found/ambiguous variants have no `.id` field); `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, confirming exhaustiveness at all 5 sites. The 3 registry_def sites (relate_application source+link-target, edit_jsonschema_non_destructive) ROLLBACK with zero mutation and a Russian human message naming the slug + listing candidate apps (slug+display name) + UUID escape-hatch instruction on ambiguous. The 2 application sites (author_binding, generate_process grounding) are provably unreachable for 'ambiguous' given UNIQUE(tenant_id, slug) on choros.application (migrations/003_application.sql:15, confirmed by direct read) — author_binding still handles it defensively (rollback+message), grounding correctly collapses ambiguous into the same null-degrade as not_found (a soft hint path, never a write, byte-identical prior behavior). registry_def is UNIQUE(tenant_id, application_id, slug) with no UNIQUE(tenant_id,slug) (migrations/004_registry_def.sql:20, confirmed) — the cross-app collision precondition is real, not hypothetical. Ran the new live-Postgres test directly against :55432 (real DB, not mocked): both AC tests pass (2/2) — AC-1/2 proves honest refusal with NO mutation to either registry's record_schema; AC-3 proves the raw-UUID escape hatch resolves exactly one registry. Also reran the neighboring T-0607 db-test (edit-jsonschema-slug-resolve.test.ts) — still green (6/6 in that filtered run), confirming the non-ambiguous path is untouched. Spec, ADR and pr-handoff are internally consistent with the diff (call-site count, message wording, schema claims all check out against the actual migrations and code). No case-content (закупка/ТЭЛ/purchaseApproval literals) appears anywhere in the diff itself — anti-case gate holds for this change. One legitimate scope finding (not a blocker, and explicitly out of scope per this task's own spec non-goals): the same slug->LIMIT-1-without-ORDER-BY pattern exists unaddressed in ~10 other files (employee, tenant, grants, sod, org, etc.) — flagged as F1 for a future task, since none of those tables are documented as having a matching cross-scope ambiguity precondition and auditing each is a separate investigation.
